images.title: Primes in a Venn diagram
images.purpose: Show that shared primes give the HCF and all primes together give the LCM, using 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 and 2 × 3 × 3 × 7.
images.composition: One two-circle Venn diagram in the centre with a number above each circle and two short result lines below, plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Left circle outlined teal #0072B2, labelled above 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.
Right circle outlined amber #E69F00, labelled above 2 × 3 × 3 × 7.
Left only part: exactly 2 prime tiles, 2 and 5.
Overlap, shaded light reddish purple #CC79A7: exactly 2 prime tiles, 2 and 3.
Right only part: exactly 2 prime tiles, 3 and 7.
So 6 tiles in all (this count is not written in the image).
Below, line one in reddish purple: HCF = 2 × 3 = 6, set just under the overlap.
Below, line two in green #009E73: LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 1260, the product of all 6 tiles.
rejection: more or fewer than 2 tiles in any of the three regions
an HCF other than 6 or an LCM other than 1260
images.takeaway: The HCF takes the primes both numbers share; the LCM takes every prime, each as often as it is needed.
images.description: A Venn diagram of the primes of 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 and 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 with 2 and 3 in the overlap, giving HCF 6 and LCM 1260.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on reading HCF and LCM from prime factorisations.
images.teaching_notes: Multiply the overlap for the HCF, then multiply every tile in the picture for the LCM.

image_decisions.why: The Venn layout shows minimum and maximum counts as regions, which is easier to see than a list.
